question: The repression of independent Belarusian journalists, including arrests and forced emigration, have intensified since 2020 as a result of the Lukashenka regime ramping up its repression. The EU has repeatedly declared that it promotes and supports the safety and work of independent journalists in its external actions and policies by providing them with, among other things, financial support.

Free Belarusian media are essential for overthrowing the Lukashenka regime and building democracy and civil society in Belarus, which should be a priority of the EU’s policies towards our eastern neighbour. In view of the above: 1.
What funds has the Commission allocated to independent Belarusian media in 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025?
Could the Commission indicate through which intermediary entity and to which independent Belarusian media outlets such funds were transferred?
Which programmes implemented by independent Belarusian media received financial support from the Commission, and what subject matter do they cover?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.2.2026) The Commission welcomes the Parliament’s continued focus on this important issue, as Belarus remains high on the political agenda. The EU is committed to supporting the people of Belarus in their path towards freedom and democracy and recognises the crucial role of independent media in this process.

Since 2020, the Commission has mobilised over EUR 38 million in support of independent media in Belarus. The EU will continue to prioritise support for independent media as reaffirmed by the Commissioner for Enlargement and the High Representative/Vice-President in their joint statement1 marking the fifth anniversary of the fraudulent 2020 elections.

In designing programmes to support Belarusian independent media, the Commission’s priority is to reach people inside the country and identify Belarusian outlets with strong organic audiences. Support is delivered through experienced implementing partners who operate competitive sub-granting processes.

These well-established organisations play a key role in supporting a diverse, healthy and competitive media ecosystem. EU assistance has supported dozens of Belarusian outlets at national, regional and local level, as well as bloggers and investigative media.

This has helped media professionals and journalists adapt to a changing repressive environment, including through more active engagement on social media and innovative communication methods. The Commission’s assistance to independent media fosters innovation in the sector by supporting experimentation with content strategies that will help target different priority audiences, including young people.
